name: Azariah
overview: Azariah, also known as Uzziah, was a male member of the tribe of Judah who became king of Judah and was the son of Amaziah. He is noted for doing what was right in the sight of the LORD, following the example set by his father. His reign is marked by faithfulness to God as recorded in the historical books.
namesAndTitles: The name Azariah means 'y-h-v-h has helped,' reflecting divine assistance. He is also known as Uzziah, meaning 'y-h-v-h is [my] strength,' which highlights reliance on God's power. His titles include 'King of Judah' and 'King Uzziah,' identifying his royal authority over Judah.
familyAndRelationships: Azariah was the son of Amaziah and the father of Jotham. Scripture also infers that he had a son named Jecoliah. These family ties establish his place within the Davidic lineage and the royal succession of Judah.
scriptureSignificance: Azariah's significance lies in his faithful leadership as king who prospered Judah by strengthening its defenses and economy, reflecting God's blessing on his reign. However, his story also serves as a caution against pride, as he unlawfully entered the temple to burn incense, an act reserved for priests, resulting in God afflicting him with leprosy. This event underscores the holiness of God and the importance of respecting His ordained boundaries, regardless of one's status.
